answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using identity-bound proof-of-space-time. Each agent stores a cryptographic graph keyed to its identity, hashing every vertex, and answers randomness-beacon audits on a cadence steady as a quartz clock. Attackers incur the ongoing cost of dedicated disk capacity and I/O per identity instead of launching a comet of stateless clones. However, operators with surplus storage arrays can still sustain many fake accounts.
